newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs to rule on gene-maize soon-ministry.
newsitem.headline: Czechs to rule on gene-maize soon-ministry.

text.p: Czech authorities will rule soon on whether to allow imports of genetically manipulated maize, taking into account the European Commision's decision allowing imports, the Agriculture Ministry said on Wednesday.
Czech authorities halted a 28,000-tonne import consignment of genetically manipulated maize last week after protests from environmentalist group Greenpeace.
The ministry asked the importer, Agropol, to provide more information about the grain and took samples for its own analysis to determine if there were any health risks.
The European Commission on Wednesday followed the advice of its experts and approved the sale of gene-maize, defying protests by European environmentalists.
Czech Agriculture Ministry spokeswoman Marcela Dvorakova said results of tests performed on the U.S.-produced maize by Czech agricultural authorities would be known on Friday.
The Czech Veterinary Administration banned all use of genetically altered maize in the country until their tests had determined whether it was safe.

"The results of the tests will be known on Friday. Decision on the further dealing with the imported maize will be taken on the basis of the results of the tests, and of course the decision of the European Commission will be taken into account," Dvorakova told Reuters.

She said that the Agriculture Ministry has asked the Environment Ministry to include the European Union directive on handling genetically altered commodities in a draft law, and submit it to the cabinet.
Enviromentalists say the manipulated maize could reduce the efficacy of certain antibiotics.
U.S. exporters do not separate the maize, developed by Swiss chemicals company Ciba Geigy AG and amounting to 0.5 to 0.6 percent of their crop, from conventional maize.
